قال الله تعالى:
 (وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُودَ سُلَيْمَانَ، نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ، إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ ۝ إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ ۝ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّي، حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِالْحِجَابِ ۝ رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ، فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْنَاقِ ۝ وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ، وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا، ثُمَّ أَنَابَ ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَّا يَنبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِي، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ) [ص: ٣٠-٣٥].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ عِلْمًا، وَقَالَا: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۝ وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ، وَقَالَ: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ الطَّيْرِ، وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْمُبِينُ) [النمل: ١٥-١٦].

collections.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said:
 “And We granted Sulayman to Dawud. Excellent was the servant; indeed, he was oft-returning. When the poised, swift horses were displayed before him in the evening, he said: Indeed, I loved the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord, until they disappeared behind the veil. Return them to me. Then he began passing his hand over their legs and necks. And We certainly tested Sulayman and placed upon his throne a body; then he returned. He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” [Ṣad: 30–35]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And We certainly gave knowledge to Dawud and Sulayman, and they said: Praise belongs to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants. And Sulayman inherited Dawud and said: O people, we have been taught the speech of birds and have been given of all things. Indeed, this is the clear favor.” [al-Naml: 15–16]

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
 (إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ، وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ، وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ، وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا) [النساء: ١٦٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَدَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ، إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ، إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ، وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ ۝ فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ، وَكُلًّا آتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا، وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُودَ الْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَالطَّيْرَ، وَكُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ ۝ وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ، لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّن بَأْسِكُمْ، فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَاكِرُونَ) [الأنبياء: ٧٨-٨٠].
وقال تعالى:
 (يَا دَاوُودُ، إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ، فَاحْكُم بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ، وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللهِ، إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ) [ص: ٢٦].

Allah Most High said:
 “Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Ibrahim, Isma‘il, Isḥaq, Ya‘qub, the Tribes, ‘Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun, and Sulayman, and We gave Dawud the Zabur.” [al-Nisa’: 163]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the field, when the sheep of a people strayed therein by night, and We were witness to their judgment. We gave understanding of it to Sulayman, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify with Dawud, and the birds also; and We were doers. And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your battle. So will you be grateful?” [al-Anbiya’: 78–80]
And Allah Most High said:
 “O Dawud, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people with truth and do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from the path of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah will have a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.” [Ṣad: 26]

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
 (وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ ۝ وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَاءِ هَٰؤُلَاءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ ۝ قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ ۝ قَالَ يَا آدَمُ أَنبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّا أَنبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ ۝ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ ۝ وَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ ۝ فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ ۖ وَقُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَاعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ ۝ فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ۝ قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) [البقرة: ٣٠-٣٨].
وقال تعالى:
 (إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَرًا مِّن طِينٍ ۝ فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ ۝ فَسَجَدَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ ۝ إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ اسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ ۝ قَالَ يَا إِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ ۖ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ الْعَالِينَ ۝ قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ ۖ خَلَقْتَنِي مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ ۝ قَالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ ۝ وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِي إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِي إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ ۝ قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنظَرِينَ ۝ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ ۝ قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ ۝ إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ ۝ قَالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ ۝ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) [ص: ٧١-٨٥].
قال ابن كثير: “فهذه أربع تشريفات: خلقُه له بيده الكريمة، ونفخُه فيه من روحه، وأمرُه الملائكة بالسجود له، وتعليمُه أسماء الأشياء”.

Allah Most High said:
 “And when your Lord said to the angels: Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successor. They said: Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption in it and shed blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You? He said: Indeed, I know what you do not know. And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He presented them to the angels and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful. They said: Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. He said: O Adam, inform them of their names. And when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you used to conceal? And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused, was arrogant, and became among the disbelievers. And We said: O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise, and eat from it freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers. Then Satan caused them to slip from it and brought them out from what they had been in. And We said: Descend, some of you enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time. Then Adam received words from his Lord, so He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful. We said: Descend from it, all of you. Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.” [al-Baqarah: 30–38]
And Allah Most High said:
 “When your Lord said to the angels: Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay. So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him in prostration. So the angels prostrated, all of them together, except Iblis; he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers. He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted? He said: I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay. He said: Then leave it, for indeed you are expelled, and indeed My curse is upon you until the Day of Judgment. He said: My Lord, then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected. He said: Indeed, you are among those given respite, until the Day of the appointed time. He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them. He said: The truth — and the truth I say — I will surely fill Hell with you and with those who follow you, all together.” [Ṣad: 71–85]
Ibn Kathir said: “These are four honors: His creating him with His noble hand, His breathing into him of His spirit, His commanding the angels to prostrate to him, and His teaching him the names of things.”
His saying in Surat al-Baqarah [31]: “And He taught Adam the names, all of them,” means the categories of names, such as heaven and earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, animals, inanimate objects, and so on. What is meant is not every individual name, because firstly they are countless, and secondly many of them had not yet been created. Thus His saying “all of them” means all the categories at that time.

قال الله تعالى:
 (وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ، فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ، وَلَا تَخَافِي وَلَا تَحْزَنِي، إِنَّا رَادُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ، وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ ۝ فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ، لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا، إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا خَاطِئِينَ ۝ وَقَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ: قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ، لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ، عَسَىٰ أَن يَنفَعَنَا أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا، وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ ۝ وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغًا، إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ، لَوْلَا أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا، لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) [القصص: ٧-١٠].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مُوسَىٰ، إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلَصًا، وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا ۝ وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنِ، وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيًّا ۝ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَا أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ نَبِيًّا) [مريم: ٥١-٥٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ، وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا) [الفرقان: ٣٥].
يقال: إن فرعون رأى في منامه رؤيا أفزعته، فدعا الكهنة والسحرة والمعبرين، فسألهم عن تأويل رؤياه، فقالوا: يولد في بني إسرائيل غلام يسلبك الملك، ويغلبك على سلطانك. فغضب وجن جنونه، وأمر بقتل كل غلام يولد لبني إسرائيل، وجند لذلك القوابل من النساء، فذبح نحو سبعين ألف ولد كما في قصص الأنبياء للثعلبي (ص ١٧٣-١٧٤)، وقد تكون فيه مبالغة. فلما وُلد موسى خافت أمه، فألهمها الله تعالى أن تلقيه في البحر، وهو النيل، إلى آخر ما ذُكر في القرآن الكريم.

 (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مُوسَىٰ، إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلَصًا، وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا ۝ وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنِ، وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيًّا ۝ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَا أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ نَبِيًّا) [مريم: ٥١-٥٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ، وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا) [الفرقان: ٣٥].
يقال: إن فرعون رأى في منامه رؤيا أفزعته، فدعا الكهنة والسحرة والمعبرين، فسألهم عن تأويل رؤياه، فقالوا: يولد في بني إسرائيل غلام يسلبك الملك، ويغلبك على سلطانك. فغضب وجن جنونه، وأمر بقتل كل غلام يولد لبني إسرائيل، وجند لذلك القوابل من النساء، فذبح نحو سبعين ألف ولد كما في قصص الأنبياء للثعلبي (ص ١٧٣-١٧٤)، وقد تكون فيه مبالغة. فلما وُلد موسى خافت أمه، فألهمها الله تعالى أن تلقيه في البحر، وهو النيل، إلى آخر ما ذُكر في القرآن الكريم.

Allah Most High said:
 “And We inspired the mother of Musa: Nurse him; then when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him among the messengers. Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a grief for them. Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers were sinners. And the wife of Pharaoh said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him. Perhaps he may benefit us, or we may take him as a son, while they perceived not. And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty; she was about to disclose him, had We not strengthened her heart so that she would be among the believers.” [al-Qaṣaṣ: 7–10]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And mention in the Book Musa. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet. We called him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near in private conversation. And We granted him, from Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet.” [Maryam: 51–53]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And We certainly gave Musa the Book and made with him his brother Harun as a minister.” [al-Furqan: 35]
It is said that Pharaoh saw a dream that terrified him. He summoned the priests, sorcerers, and interpreters, and asked them about the interpretation of his dream. They said: A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will strip you of kingship and overcome your authority. So he became angry and enraged, and ordered that every boy born to the Children of Israel be killed. He appointed midwives from among the women for that purpose, and about seventy thousand children were slaughtered, as mentioned in Qiṣaṣ al-Anbiya’ by al-Tha‘labi (p. 173–174), though there may be exaggeration in it. When Musa was born, his mother feared for him, so Allah Most High inspired her to cast him into the river, meaning the Nile, and the rest of what is mentioned in the Noble Qur’an occurred.

إذا كان أول بيت وضع بمكة، فيلزم منه أن يكون أول إنسان وجد في مكة أيضًا. فالله تعالى أعلم، قد يكون آدم عليه السلام أُنزل بمكة، وأمر ببناء أول بيت للعبادة. ولما اندثر هذا البيت، ولم يبق منه إلا قواعده، أمر الله تعالى إبراهيم عليه السلام بإعادة بناء هذا البيت على القواعد التي وضعها آدم عليه السلام، كما قال الله تعالى:
 (وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ، رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) [البقرة: ١٢٧].

Allah Most High said:
 “Indeed, the first House established for people was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.” [Al ‘Imran: 96]
If the first House was established in Makkah, then it follows that the first human being was also found in Makkah. Allah Most High knows best. It may be that Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down in Makkah and commanded to build the first House for worship. When this House disappeared and nothing remained of it except its foundations, Allah Most High commanded Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to rebuild this House upon the foundations that Adam, peace be upon him, had placed, as Allah Most High said:
 “And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, along with Isma‘il, saying: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.” [al-Baqarah: 127]
 As for the texts reported specifically on this matter, none of them are established.

Allah Most High said:
 “And We gave him Isḥaq and Ya‘qub; each We guided. And Nuh We guided before; and among his descendants were Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun; and thus do We reward the doers of good. And Zakariyya, Yaḥya, ‘Isa, and Ilyas — each was of the righteous. And Isma‘il, al-Yasa‘, Yunus, and Luṭ — each We favored over the worlds. And from among their fathers, their descendants, and their brothers, We chose them and guided them to a straight path. That is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. If they had associated partners, all that they used to do would have become worthless for them. Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book, judgment, and prophethood. But if these people disbelieve in it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it. Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance. Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it; it is only a reminder for the worlds.” [al-An‘am: 84–90]

chapters.title_en: 3 — Chapter: The Prophet ﷺ Following the Example of Dawud, Peace Be upon Him

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى: (قَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ابْنَتَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ عَلَى أَنْ تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) [القصص: ٢٧].
وأما ما رُوي عن عتبة بن النُدَّر قال: كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ فقرأ طسم، حتى إذا بلغ قصة موسى قال: ((إن موسى ﷺ أجَّر نفسه ثماني سنين أو عشرًا على عفة فرجه وطعام بطنه)). فهو ضعيف جدًا.
رواه ابن ماجه (٢٤٤٤)، وابن قانع في معجم الصحابة (٢/٢٦٩)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/١٣٥) كلهم من طريق محمد بن مصفّى، نا بقية بن الوليد، عن مسلمة بن علي، عن سعيد بن أبي أيوب، عن الحارث بن يزيد، عن علي بن رباح، عن عتبة بن الندر.
وفيه مسلمة بن علي الخشني وهو متروك، والراوي عنه بقية بن الوليد مدلس وعنعن.
ورُوي أيضًا عن عتبة بن الندر السلمي من وجه آخر بلفظ أطول في وفاء موسى الأجل، وهو ضعيف أيضًا.
رواه ابن أبي عاصم في الآحاد والمثاني (١٣٧٨)، وابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٩/٢٩٧٠) — والسياق له —، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/١٣٤)، كلهم من طرق عن ابن لهيعة، عن الحارث بن يزيد الحضرمي، عن علي بن رباح اللخمي، عن عتبة بن الندر السلمي.
وابن لهيعة معروف بسوء حفظه، والرواة عنه ليسوا من العبادلة الذين تحمل أهل العلم روايتهم عنه.

Allah Most High said: “He said: Indeed, I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be from you. I do not wish to make things difficult for you. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous.” [al-Qasas: 27]
As for what is reported from ‘Utbah ibn al-Nudarr that the Prophet ﷺ said Musa hired himself for eight or ten years for the sake of preserving his chastity and obtaining food, it is very weak.
It was narrated by Ibn Majah (2444), Ibn Qani‘ in Mu‘jam al-Sahabah (2/269), and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (17/135) through Muhammad ibn Musaffa, from Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, from Maslamah ibn ‘Ali, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from ‘Ali ibn Rabah, from ‘Utbah ibn al-Nudarr.
In this chain is Maslamah ibn ‘Ali al-Khushani, who is abandoned, while Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid is a mudallis and narrated it with ‘an‘anah.
A longer report from ‘Utbah ibn al-Nudarr al-Sulami concerning Musa completing his term is also weak.
It was narrated by Ibn Abi ‘Asim in al-Ahad wa al-Mathani (1378), Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir (9/2970), whose wording this is, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (17/134), through routes from Ibn Lahi‘ah, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from ‘Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, from ‘Utbah ibn al-Nudarr al-Sulami.
Ibn Lahi‘ah is well known for poor memory, and the narrators from him here are not among the ‘Abadilah whose transmission from him the scholars accepted.

 “They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing Fire. So they intended against him a plot, but We made them the lowest.” [al-Ṣaffat: 97–98]

Allah Most High said:
 “He said: Indeed, I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, then that is from you. chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
 (هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ، قَالَ: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً، إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ ۝ فَنَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ، وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرَابِ: أَنَّ اللهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ، مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ اللهِ، وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا، وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) [آل عمران: ٣٨-٣٩].
وقال الله تعالى:
 (كهيعص ۝ ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيَّا ۝ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ نِدَاءً خَفِيًّا ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ، إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي، وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا، وَلَمْ أَكُن بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا ۝ وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ مِن وَرَائِي، وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا، فَهَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا ۝ يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ، وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا ۝ يَا زَكَرِيَّا، إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيَىٰ، لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ، أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ، وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا، وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا ۝ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ: هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ، وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ، وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ، اجْعَل لِّي آيَةً. قَالَ: آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا ۝ فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ مِنَ الْمِحْرَابِ، فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا) [مريم: ١-١١].

Allah Most High said:
 “There Zakariyya called upon his Lord. He said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication. So the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber: Allah gives you glad tidings of Yaḥya, confirming a word from Allah, noble, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.” [Al ‘Imran: 38–39]
And Allah Most High said:
 “Kaf-Ha-Ya-‘Ayn-Ṣad. A mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya, when he called upon his Lord with a quiet call. He said: My Lord, my bones have weakened, my head has flared with gray hair, and never have I been disappointed in my supplication to You, my Lord. Indeed, I fear the relatives after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya‘qub, and make him, my Lord, pleasing. O Zakariyya, We give you glad tidings of a boy whose name is Yaḥya; We have not given this name to anyone before. He said: My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age? He said: Thus has your Lord said: It is easy for Me, and I created you before when you were nothing. He said: My Lord, make for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound. So he came out to his people from the chamber and signaled to them to glorify Allah morning and evening.” [Maryam: 1–11]

chapters.intro_ar_source:
لم يَرِدْ في الأحاديث الصحيحة موضع دفن عيسى عليه السلام، وأما ما رُوي عن محمد بن يوسف بن عبد الله بن سلام، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: مكتوب في التوراة صفة محمد ﷺ، وعيسى بن مريم يُدفن معه. فهو ضعيف.
رواه الترمذي (٣٦١٧) عن زيد بن أخزم الطائي البصري، حدثنا أبو قتيبة سلم بن قتيبة، حدثني أبو مودود المدني، حدثنا عثمان بن الضحاك، عن محمد بن يوسف بن عبد الله بن سلام، عن أبيه، عن جده فذكره. قال أبو مودود: وقد بقي في البيت موضع قبر.
قال الترمذي: ((هذا حديث حسن غريب، هكذا قال عثمان بن الضحاك، والمعروف الضحاك بن عثمان المديني)). قال ابن حجر: وقع في اسمه القلب.
قلت: ليس بحسن، بل ضعيف. قال البخاري: هذا الحديث لا يصح عندي، ولا يُتابع عليه. التاريخ الكبير (١/٢٦٣). وقال أبو داود عن الضحاك بن عثمان: ثقة، وابنه عثمان بن الضحاك ضعيف. وهو مع ذلك موقوف على عبد الله بن سلام.
ورُوي هذا الحديث بلفظ آخر: يُدفن عيسى عليه السلام مع رسول الله ﷺ وصاحبيه، فيكون قبره رابعًا. وهو ضعيف أيضًا.
رواه الطبراني، ومن طريقه المزي في تهذيب الكمال (٤٤١٤)، من وجه آخر عن عثمان بن الضحاك بإسناده، وهو موقوف أيضًا.
والحديث رُوي أيضًا عن عائشة مرفوعًا، ولا يصح إسناده كما قال ابن كثير في البداية والنهاية (٢/٩٦).

No authentic hadith establishes the place where ‘Isa, peace be upon him, will be buried. As for what is reported from Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Salam, from his father, from his grandfather, that the description of Muhammad ﷺ is written in the Torah and that ‘Isa ibn Maryam will be buried with him, it is weak.
Al-Tirmidhi (3617) narrated it through Zayd ibn Akhzam al-Ta’i al-Basri, from Abu Qutaybah Salm ibn Qutaybah, from Abu Mawdud al-Madani, from ‘Uthman ibn al-Dahhak, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Salam, from his father, from his grandfather. Abu Mawdud added: “There remains in the chamber a place for a grave.”
Al-Tirmidhi said: “This is a hasan gharib hadith. This is how ‘Uthman ibn al-Dahhak was named, while what is known is al-Dahhak ibn ‘Uthman al-Madani.” Ibn Hajar said that the name had been reversed.
I say: It is not hasan; rather, it is weak. Al-Bukhari said: “This hadith is not authentic in my view, and he is not followed in it.” Al-Tarikh al-Kabir (1/263). Abu Dawud said that al-Dahhak ibn ‘Uthman is trustworthy, whereas his son ‘Uthman ibn al-Dahhak is weak. Moreover, the report is mawquf upon ‘Abdullah ibn Salam.
This report was also narrated with another wording: that ‘Isa, peace be upon him, will be buried with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two Companions, making his grave the fourth. This is also weak.
Al-Tabarani narrated it, and through him al-Mizzi in Tahdhib al-Kamal (4414), through another route from ‘Uthman ibn al-Dahhak with the same chain; it too is mawquf.
The report was also narrated from ‘A’ishah as marfu‘, but its chain is not authentic, as Ibn Kathir stated in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (2/96).

 (وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِي وَتَذْكِيرِي بِآيَاتِ اللهِ فَعَلَى اللهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ، فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ ۝ فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ، إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللهِ، وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ۝ فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ، وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ خَلَائِفَ، وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا، فَانظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُنذَرِينَ) [يونس: ٧١-٧٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ: إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ ۝ أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللهَ، إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ ۝ فَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن قَوْمِهِ: مَا نَرَاكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا، وَمَا نَرَاكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ الرَّأْيِ، وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍ، بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَاذِبِينَ ۝ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّي، وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ، فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ، أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمْ لَهَا كَارِهُونَ) [هود: ٢٥-٢٨].

Allah Most High said:
 “And recite to them the news of Nuh, when he said to his people: O my people, if my standing among you and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has become burdensome to you, then upon Allah I have relied. So gather your plan and your partners, then let not your plan be obscure to you; then carry it out against me and do not give me respite. But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only upon Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims. But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So look how was the end of those who were warned.” [Yunus: 71–73]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And We certainly sent Nuh to his people: Indeed, I am to you a clear warner, that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day. So the chiefs who disbelieved from among his people said: We do not see you except as a human like us, and we do not see that any have followed you except the lowest among us, at first glance, and we do not see in you any merit over us; rather, we think you are liars. He said: O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you, shall we force it upon you while you dislike it?” [Hud: 25–28]

It is reported from Abu Musa that the Prophet ﷺ received a Bedouin generously and told him to come back. When he returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ask for what you need.” He asked for a she-camel to ride and goats for his family to milk. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Are you unable to be like the old woman of the Children of Israel?”
He said: “When Musa traveled with the Children of Israel from Egypt, they lost the way. Their scholars said that when Yusuf was about to die, he took a covenant from them by Allah that they would not leave Egypt until they carried his bones with them. Musa asked who knew the location of his grave, and they said an old woman from the Children of Israel. She would only guide him if he granted her request: to be with him in Paradise. Allah revealed to him to grant her request. She led them to a pool of stagnant water, had them drain it, dig, and bring out the bones of Yusuf. When they raised them onto the ground, the road became as bright as daylight.”
It was narrated by Abu Ya‘la (7254), through him Ibn Hibban (723), and al-Hakim (2/404–405, 571–572), through routes from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa. Al-Hakim authenticated the chain.
I say: Outwardly the chain appears free of defect and Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq’s hearing from Abu Burdah is established, yet the meaning contains strangeness: how could Yusuf’s grave have been unknown to Musa, a messenger receiving revelation, until an old woman guided him to it? Why would the grave have been in stagnant water? And would nothing of his body have remained except bones, when an authentic hadith states that the earth does not consume the bodies of the prophets?
Ibn Kathir said after narrating the story: “This hadith is extremely strange, and it is more likely mawquf.”
I say: Perhaps Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari received it from some of the Jews.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
 (وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ فِي مَوْجٍ كَالْجِبَالِ، وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ، وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ: يَا بُنَيَّ ارْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ الْكَافِرِينَ ۝ قَالَ سَآوِي إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الْمَاءِ. قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ. وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا الْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُغْرَقِينَ ۝ وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ، وَيَا سَمَاءُ أَقْلِعِي، وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ، وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ، وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ، وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ ۝ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ رَّبَّهُ فَقَالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي، وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ الْحَقُّ، وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ الْحَاكِمِينَ ۝ قَالَ يَا نُوحُ، إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ، إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ، فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ، إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ، إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ، وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي أَكُن مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ) [هود: ٤٢-٤٧].

 وفيه الحسن مدلس ولم يصرح، وإن كان بعض أهل العلم ذهبوا إلى سماعه من عمران بن الحصين.

 (وَفِي عَادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ ۝ مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَيْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَالرَّمِيمِ) [الذاريات: ٤١-٤٢].
وقال تعالى:
 (كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ، فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ ۝ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ ۝ تَنزِعُ النَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ ۝ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ ۝ وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ، فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ) [القمر: ١٨-٢٢].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ ۝ سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا، فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ ۝ فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ) [الحاقة: ٦-٨].

Allah Most High said:
 “And in ‘Ad, when We sent against them the barren wind. It left nothing of what it came upon except that it made it like decayed ruins.” [al-Dhariyat: 41–42]
And Allah Most High said:
 “‘Ad denied, so how were My punishment and My warnings? Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune, uprooting people as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees. So how were My punishment and My warnings? And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?” [al-Qamar: 18–22]
And Allah Most High said:
 “As for ‘Ad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind, which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession; so you would see the people therein fallen, as though they were hollow trunks of palm trees. So do you see any remnant of them?” [al-Haqqah: 6–8]

Allah Most High said:
 “And to Thamud, their brother Ṣaliḥ. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity besides Him. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you, so leave her to eat in Allah’s land and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you.” [al-A‘raf: 73]
Thamud was a well-known tribe traced back to their forefather Thamud ibn ‘Amir ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh. They were Arabs from the ancient Arabs and lived in al-Ḥijr, between the Hijaz and Tabuk. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by it.

قال الله تعالى:
 (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ، سَيَهْدِينِ ۝ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ ۝ فَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ ۝ فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ، قَالَ: يَا بُنَيَّ، إِنِّي أَرَىٰ فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ، فَانظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ. قَالَ: يَا أَبَتِ، افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ، سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ ۝ فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ ۝ وَنَادَيْنَاهُ أَن يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ ۝ قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيَا، إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ ۝ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ الْبَلَاءُ الْمُبِينُ ۝ وَفَدَيْنَاهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ) [الصافات: ٩٩-١٠٧].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَامْرَأَتُهُ قَائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ، فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ، وَمِن وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ) [هود: ٧١].

Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.” [al-Ṣaffat: 99–107]

 “And his wife was standing, and she laughed. So We gave her glad tidings of Isḥaq, and after Isḥaq, Ya‘qub.” [Hud: 71]

قال الله تعالى:
 (وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ ۝ وَبَارَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰ إِسْحَاقَ، وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ) [الصافات: ١١٢-١١٣].

Allah Most High said:
 “And We gave him glad tidings of Isḥaq, a prophet from among the righteous. And We blessed him and Isḥaq. And among their descendants are those who do good and those clearly wronging themselves.” [al-Ṣaffat: 112–113]
This glad tiding came from the angels to Ibrahim and Sarah when they passed by them on their way to the towns of the people of Luṭ, to destroy them because of their disbelief and wickedness.
And Allah Most High said:
 “Our messengers certainly came to Ibrahim with glad tidings. They said: Peace. He said: Peace, and he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf. But when he saw that their hands did not reach toward it, he found them strange and felt fear from them. They said: Do not fear; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Luṭ. And his wife was standing, and she laughed. So We gave her glad tidings of Isḥaq, and after Isḥaq, Ya‘qub. She said: Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is a wondrous thing. They said: Do you marvel at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.” [Hud: 69–73]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And We gave him Isḥaq and Ya‘qub; each We guided. And Nuh We guided before; and among his descendants were Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun. And thus do We reward the doers of good.” [al-An‘am: 84]

قال الله تعالى:
 (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ، وَجَاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرَىٰ، يُجَادِلُنَا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ ۝ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُّنِيبٌ ۝ يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ، أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا، إِنَّهُ قَدْ جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ، وَإِنَّهُمْ آتِيهِمْ عَذَابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ ۝ وَلَمَّا جَاءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا، سِيءَ بِهِمْ، وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا، وَقَالَ: هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ ۝ وَجَاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ، وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ. قَالَ: يَا قَوْمِ، هَٰؤُلَاءِ بَنَاتِي، هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ، فَاتَّقُوا اللهَ، وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِي ضَيْفِي، أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ ۝ قَالُوا لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِي بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ، وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ ۝ قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً، أَوْ آوِي إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ ۝ قَالُوا يَا لُوطُ، إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ، لَن يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ، فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ، وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ، إِنَّهُ مُصِيبُهَا مَا أَصَابَهُمْ، إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ الصُّبْحُ، أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ ۝ فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا، جَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا، وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ مَّنضُودٍ ۝ مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ، وَمَا هِيَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ) [هود: ٧٤-٨٣].

Allah Most High said:
 “When fear had left Ibrahim and the glad tidings had come to him, he argued with Us concerning the people of Luṭ. Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing, often sighing in supplication, and repentant. ومن أخباره عليه السلام أنه لما جعله الملك من خاصته وأهل مشورته، حتى أصبح يوسف عليه السلام من كبار شخصيات مصر:
١- طلب من الملك أن يجعله وزيرًا لخزانة الدولة:
(وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي، فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ: إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ ۝ قَالَ: اجْعَلْنِي عَلَىٰ خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ، إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ) [يوسف: ٥٤-٥٥].
قوله: (اجْعَلْنِي عَلَىٰ خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ) أي على خزائن أرض مصر، فإن يوسف عليه السلام طلب من الملك أن يعينه وزيرًا للمالية، وعرّف نفسه بأنه أمين في حفظ أموال الدولة، وعليم في تصريفها وإنفاقها، فقبل منه الملك، وولاه على خزانة مصر.
٢- صواع يوسف عليه السلام نُسب إلى الملك.
(فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ، جَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ، ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ: أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ، إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ ۝ قَالُوا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ: مَّاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ ۝ قَالُوا: نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ، وَلِمَن جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ، وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ) [يوسف: ٧٠-٧٢].
قوله: (السِّقَايَةَ): وهي إناء من فضة، كان يكيل للناس به الطعام.

٣- صار يوسف عليه السلام عزيز مصر.
(قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ، إِنَّ لَهُ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا، فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ، إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) [يوسف: ٧٨].

قوله: (الْعَزِيزُ) قيل: هو لقب ملوك مصر في ذلك الوقت، وقيل: هو كل من له منزلة عالية ورفيعة في الدولة، كالوزير ومستشار الملك وغيرهما.

 وقوله: (فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ) أي أعطنا بهذا الثمن القليل ما كنت تعطينا قبل ذلك.

 وقد استنبط بعض أهل العلم من هذه الآية الكريمة أن الصدقة لم تُحرّم على الأنبياء السابقين عليهم الصلاة والسلام، وعلى آلهم مثل ما حُرّمت على نبينا محمد ﷺ وعلى آله.
٤- كان ليوسف عليه السلام عرش.
(وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ، وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا، وَقَالَ: يَا أَبَتِ، هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُؤْيَايَ مِن قَبْلُ، قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقًّا، وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ السِّجْنِ، وَجَاءَ بِكُم مِّنَ الْبَدْوِ، مِن بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ الشَّيْطَانُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي، إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَاءُ، إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ) [يوسف: ١٠٠].
العرش: مجلس خاص للملك.
 قوله: (وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا): المراد بالسجود هنا هو الانحناء والتواضع، وهي تحية الناس يومئذ، وليس المراد وضع الجباه على الأرض.
٥- إن الله مكّن يوسف عليه السلام في الأرض.
(وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِن تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ، وَاللهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰ أَمْرِهِ، وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) [يوسف: ٢١].
(وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ، نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَاءُ، وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) [يوسف: ٥٦].
قوله: (فِي الْأَرْضِ) أي في أرض مصر.
 وقوله: (يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ) أي يتصرف فيها كيف يشاء.
٦- ثم دعا الله عز وجل:
(رَبِّ، قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ، وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ، فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، أَنتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا، وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ) [يوسف: ١٠١].
يعني بعد المراحل المذكورة صار يوسف عليه السلام ملكًا على أرض مصر، وكان هذا آخر دعائه بعد أن تمت النعمة عليه باجتماعه بأبويه وإخوته، وما منّ الله عليه من النبوة والملك.
 قوله: (وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ): هم آباؤه وإخوته من الأنبياء والمرسلين.
 قوله: (تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا): أي توفني على الإسلام والإيمان.
وقال بعض السلف: إن يوسف عليه السلام أول من تمنى الموت من الأنبياء.
 قلت: إنما فيه تمني الموت على الإسلام، وهذا مشروع لجميع المسلمين، وليس فيه دعاء باستعجال الموت؛ لأن صيغة الأمر إنما تدل على المستقبل إلا إذا قُرنت بـ “الآن”، فتدل على الحال.

(وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ، نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَاءُ، وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) [يوسف: ٥٦].
قوله: (فِي الْأَرْضِ) أي في أرض مصر.
 وقوله: (يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ) أي يتصرف فيها كيف يشاء.
٦- ثم دعا الله عز وجل:
(رَبِّ، قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ، وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ، فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، أَنتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا، وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ) [يوسف: ١٠١].
يعني بعد المراحل المذكورة صار يوسف عليه السلام ملكًا على أرض مصر، وكان هذا آخر دعائه بعد أن تمت النعمة عليه باجتماعه بأبويه وإخوته، وما منّ الله عليه من النبوة والملك.
 قوله: (وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ): هم آباؤه وإخوته من الأنبياء والمرسلين.
 قوله: (تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا): أي توفني على الإسلام والإيمان.
وقال بعض السلف: إن يوسف عليه السلام أول من تمنى الموت من الأنبياء.
 قلت: إنما فيه تمني الموت على الإسلام، وهذا مشروع لجميع المسلمين، وليس فيه دعاء باستعجال الموت؛ لأن صيغة الأمر إنما تدل على المستقبل إلا إذا قُرنت بـ “الآن”، فتدل على الحال.
 وقد قال السحرة الذين آمنوا بموسى عليه السلام لما هددهم فرعون بالقتل والصلب: (رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا، وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ) [الأعراف: ١٢٦].

He is Yusuf ibn Ya‘qub ibn Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim, the Close Friend of Allah, and all of them were prophets. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed an entire surah about Yusuf, peace be upon him. It contains many lessons, reflections, and admonitions. His story is among the best of stories, as Allah Most High said:
 “We relate to you the best of stories through what We have revealed to you of this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” [Yusuf: 3]
Among the reports concerning him, peace be upon him, is that when the king made him one of his close advisers and people of counsel, Yusuf, peace be upon him, became one of the leading figures of Egypt.
1 — He asked the king to appoint him as minister over the state treasury:
“And the king said: Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself. Then when he spoke to him, he said: Indeed, today you are established and trusted with us. He said: Appoint me over the storehouses of the land; indeed, I am a knowledgeable guardian.” [Yusuf: 54–55]
His saying, “Appoint me over the storehouses of the land,” means over the storehouses of the land of Egypt. Yusuf, peace be upon him, asked the king to appoint him as minister of finance, and he described himself as trustworthy in preserving the wealth of the state and knowledgeable in managing and spending it. The king accepted that from him and placed him over the treasury of Egypt.
2 — Yusuf’s measuring cup, peace be upon him, was attributed to the king.
“When he had supplied them with their supplies, he placed the drinking vessel in his brother’s saddlebag. Then a caller called out: O caravan, indeed you are thieves. They turned toward them and said: What are you missing? They said: We are missing the king’s measuring cup, and whoever brings it will have a camel-load, and I am responsible for it.” [Yusuf: 70–72]
His saying, “the drinking vessel”: it was a vessel of silver with which he measured food for the people.
 His saying, “in the saddlebag”: it belonged to Binyamin, Yusuf’s full brother.
3 — Yusuf, peace be upon him, became the ‘Aziz of Egypt.
“They said: O ‘Aziz, indeed he has an old father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good.” [Yusuf: 78]
“When they entered upon him, they said: O ‘Aziz, hardship has touched us and our family, and we have come with poor merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.” [Yusuf: 88]
His saying, “al-‘Aziz”: it was said that this was the title of the kings of Egypt at that time. It was also said that it refers to anyone who holds a high and elevated position in the state, such as a minister, royal adviser, and the like.
 His saying, “poor merchandise”: meaning, we have come with a small price; the root meaning of izja’ is something little and inferior.
 His saying, “give us full measure”: meaning, give us for this small price what you used to give us before.
 His saying, “be charitable to us”: meaning, favor us with the difference between the good price and the inferior price, and do not reduce our measure. Charity here means something for which reward and recompense are sought.
It is narrated that al-Hasan al-Basri heard a man saying: “O Allah, give charity to me.” He said: Allah does not give charity; rather, charity is given by one who seeks reward and recompense. Instead say: “O Allah, give me,” or “show favor to me.”
 Some scholars derived from this noble verse that charity was not forbidden to the previous prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, nor to their families, as it was forbidden to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his family.
4 — Yusuf, peace be upon him, had a throne.
“And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. He said: O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true. He has been good to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.” [Yusuf: 100]
The throne is the special seat of a king.
 His saying, “and they fell down before him in prostration”: what is meant by prostration here is bowing and showing humility. It was the greeting of people at that time; what is not meant is placing the foreheads on the ground.
5 — Allah Established Yusuf, Peace Be upon Him, in the Land
“And thus We established Yusuf in the land, and so that We might teach him the interpretation of events. Allah is dominant over His affair, but most people do not know.” [Yusuf: 21]
“And thus We established Yusuf in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We grant Our mercy to whom We will, and We do not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.” [Yusuf: 56]
His saying, “in the land,” means in the land of Egypt.
 His saying, “to settle therein wherever he willed,” means he had authority to manage affairs in it as he wished.
6 — Then He Supplicated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“My Lord, You have given me of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.” [Yusuf: 101]
This means that after the stages mentioned, Yusuf, peace be upon him, became king over the land of Egypt. This was his final supplication after the blessing upon him was completed through his reunion with his parents and brothers, and through what Allah had bestowed upon him of prophethood and authority.
 His saying, “and join me with the righteous,” refers to his forefathers and brothers among the prophets and messengers.
 His saying, “Cause me to die as a Muslim,” means: cause me to die upon Islam and faith.
Some of the early scholars said that Yusuf, peace be upon him, was the first of the prophets to wish for death.
 I say: What is in it is only wishing for death upon Islam. This is lawful for all Muslims, and it is not a supplication to hasten death, because the command form refers to the future unless it is connected to “now,” in which case it refers to the present.
 The magicians who believed in Musa, peace be upon him, said when Pharaoh threatened them with killing and crucifixion: “Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims.” [al-A‘raf: 126]

وأيوب عليه السلام من ذرية إبراهيم عليه السلام، فإن قوله تعالى: (وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ، كُلًّا هَدَيْنَا، وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنَا مِن قَبْلُ، وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ، وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) [الأنعام: ٨٤] أن الضمير عائد إلى إبراهيم دون نوح.
 قال أهل السير: هو رجل من الروم، وهو أيوب بن موص بن رازح بن عيص بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم. هكذا قال ابن إسحاق، كما ذكره ابن جرير الطبري في تاريخه (١/٣٢٢).
وقال تعالى:
 (وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ: أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ، وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) [الأنبياء: ٨٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا أَيُّوبَ، إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ: أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ) [ص: ٤١].

Ayyub, peace be upon him, was from the descendants of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, because in Allah Most High’s saying: “And We gave him Isḥaq and Ya‘qub; each We guided. And Nuh We guided before; and among his descendants were Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun. And thus do We reward the doers of good” [al-An‘am: 84], the pronoun returns to Ibrahim, not Nuh.
 The historians said: He was a man from the Romans, and he was Ayyub ibn Mūṣ ibn Raziḥ ibn ‘Īṣ ibn Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim. This is what Ibn Isḥaq said, as Ibn Jarir al-Tabari mentioned in his History (1/322).
And Allah Most High said:
 “And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.” [al-Anbiya’: 83]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment.” [Ṣad: 41]

قال الله تعالى:
 (وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ ۝ إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ ۝ فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ ۝ فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ ۝ فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ ۝ لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ ۝ فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ ۝ وَأَنبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِّن يَقْطِينٍ ۝ وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ ۝ فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ) [الصافات: ١٣٩-١٤٨].

Allah Most High said:
 “And indeed Yunus was among the messengers, when he fled to the laden ship. He drew lots and was among those overcome. Then the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected. So We cast him onto the open shore while he was ill. And We caused a plant of gourd to grow over him. And We sent him to one hundred thousand or more. So they believed, and We granted them enjoyment for a time.” [al-Ṣaffat: 139–148]
And Allah Most High said:
 “And Dhul-Nun, when he went away angry and thought that We would not restrict him, then he called out in the darknesses: There is no god except You; glory be to You; indeed, I was among the wrongdoers. So We responded to him and saved him from distress. And thus do We save the believers.” [al-Anbiya’: 87–88]
The people of tafsir said: Allah sent Yunus, peace be upon him, to the people of Nineveh in the land of Mosul in Iraq. He called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but they denied him. When that matter with them became prolonged for him, he left from among them and warned them that punishment would come upon them after three days. When he left from among them and they became certain that punishment would descend upon them, Allah placed repentance and turning back in their hearts. They supplicated to Allah, Glorified and Most High, to remove the punishment from them, and Allah answered their supplication:
 “If only there had been a town that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus. When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.” [Yunus: 98]
 So Allah lifted the punishment from them, and they were “one hundred thousand or more” [al-Ṣaffat: 147]. As for Yunus, peace be upon him:
 “Then the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.” [al-Ṣaffat: 142–144]
 This event occurred in the Roman Sea at the port of Jaffa when Yunus, peace be upon him, wanted to go to Tarshish.
